title: Employment support is being redesigned as a portfolio of user-informed experiments whose legitimacy depends on learning, accessibility, and scale
source_unit: UK Department for Work and Pensions, Pathways to Work Innovation Fund applicant bid pack
geography: United Kingdom; UK-wide employment, health, skills, disability, and long-term-condition support innovation fund

observations.period: September 2026; employment support as an innovation portfolio

denominator.unit: UK Pathways to Work Innovation Fund design

fund_size.unit: million pounds available over two years

target_outcomes.value: move towards work, enter work, stay in work, and progress in work

learning_goal.value: projects must build evidence about what works and for whom, with potential for adoption, replication, or scale

observations.method: Official DWP grant-programme design and applicant guidance; this is a funding architecture, not evidence that funded interventions have yet produced outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: The eventual portfolio, participant mix, intervention quality, evaluation designs, and scale decisions are not yet known.
observations.subgroup: Disabled people and people with long-term health conditions, employers, charities, social enterprises, public bodies, researchers, and delivery partnerships.
observations.counterinterpretation: A portfolio can diversify experimentation, but fragmented short projects may create evidence that is difficult to compare, sustain, or transfer into mainstream provision.

observations.period: September 2026; lived experience and user-informed service design

denominator.unit: Pathways to Work Innovation Fund application criteria

design_requirement.value: applicants must show how lived experience of disability or long-term health conditions, user needs, and stakeholder insight informed design

accessibility_route.value: online, PDF, large print, easy read, British Sign Language, audio, Braille, Welsh, and reasonable-adjustment routes are specified

co_design.value: user research and co-design activities are eligible project costs

observations.method: Review of the fund’s applicant requirements, eligible costs, accessibility provisions, and assessment criteria.
observations.uncertainty: A requirement to describe lived-experience input does not prove that participants control decisions, are compensated fairly, or influence funded delivery.
observations.subgroup: Disabled applicants and participants, people with long-term conditions, user researchers, community organisations, and people needing accessible public-funding processes.
observations.counterinterpretation: Formal accessibility and co-design requirements may improve fit, but they can also become compliance language if commissioners privilege deliverability or scale over participant agency.

denominator.unit: eligible-organisation and partnership model in the fund guidance

eligible_sector_set.value: charities, social enterprises, businesses, researchers, public-sector organisations, local and mayoral authorities, and consortia can apply

system_joining.value: new partnerships or ways of working that join employment, health, and skills support are explicitly in scope

partnership_directory.value: a directory is intended to connect organisations with complementary lived experience, expertise, local knowledge, and delivery capability

observations.method: Analysis of official fund architecture, eligibility rules, partnership directory, and stated system objectives.
observations.uncertainty: Partnership formation, power-sharing, local coverage, and the durability of cross-sector coordination remain prospective.
observations.subgroup: Local authorities, employers, health and skills providers, voluntary organisations, researchers, disabled people, and communities with limited access to joined-up support.
observations.counterinterpretation: Broad eligibility can widen innovation, but it can also advantage organisations with grant-writing capacity and create accountability gaps across consortia.

related_sources.claim: Official landing page and fund publication context.

boundary: This record adds an institutional-learning route from disability and health-related employment barriers through lived-experience design, accessible participation, cross-sector partnerships, evidence generation, and potential scale. It does not establish funded-project outcomes, causal employment effects, participant control, or successful adoption.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official GOV.UK applicant bid pack reviewed for fund size, objectives, eligible outcomes, lived-experience and co-design criteria, accessibility routes, partnership architecture, learning requirements, and implementation timetable.
